objective: Does coding skill carry beyond Python and Terraform? Same three jobs (merge, parse, fix) in Go, Rust, PowerShell and AutoHotkey v2, executed for real.

tasks.prompt: Write a Go file (package main, no main function, no tests) that defines `func Merge(intervals [][]int) [][]int`. It merges overlapping or touching [start, end] intervals and returns them sorted by start. An empty input returns an empty slice. Output only one go code block containing the complete file.

Write a Go file (package main, no main function) defining `func ParseKV(text string) map[string]string`. Each line is key=value. Trim spaces around keys and values. Ignore blank lines, lines whose first non-space character is #, and lines without '='. A later duplicate key overrides an earlier one. Output only one go code block containing the complete file.

Write a Rust source file (standard library only, no fn main, no tests) that defines `pub fn merge(intervals: Vec<Vec<i32>>) -> Vec<Vec<i32>>`. It merges overlapping or touching [start, end] intervals and returns them sorted by start. An empty input returns an empty Vec. Output only one rust code block containing the complete file.

Write a Rust source file (standard library only, no fn main) defining `pub fn parse_kv(text: &str) -> std::collections::HashMap<String, String>`. Each line is key=value. Trim spaces around keys and values. Ignore blank lines, lines whose first non-space character is #, and lines without '='. A later duplicate key overrides an earlier one. Output only one rust code block containing the complete file.

Write PowerShell 7 code (function definitions only, no top-level code) defining `Merge-Interval` with a parameter `-Intervals`, an array of two-element arrays @(start,end). It merges overlapping or touching intervals, sorts by start, and outputs one string per merged interval formatted `start-end` (for example `1-6`). Output only one powershell code block containing the complete file.

Write PowerShell 7 code (function definitions only, no top-level code) defining `ConvertFrom-KeyValue` with a string parameter `-Text` that returns a hashtable. Each line is key=value. Trim spaces around keys and values. Ignore blank lines, lines whose first non-space character is #, and lines without '='. A later duplicate key overrides an earlier one. Output only one powershell code block containing the complete file.
tasks.harness:
. "$PSScriptRoot\solution.ps1"
$h = ConvertFrom-KeyValue -Text "# c`n a = 1 `n`nb=two words`na=3`n  # x`nbad line`n"
if ($h.Count -ne 2 -or $h['a'] -ne '3' -or $h['b'] -ne 'two words') { Write-Output 'FAIL'; exit 1 }
Write-Output 'OK'

tasks.prompt: Write AutoHotkey v2 code (function definitions only, no top-level code, no #Requires line) defining `MergeIntervals(intervals)`, where intervals is an Array of two-element Arrays [start, end]. It returns an Array of merged [start, end] Arrays sorted by start, merging overlapping or touching intervals. An empty input returns an empty Array. Output only one autohotkey code block containing the complete file.

Write AutoHotkey v2 code (function definitions only, no top-level code, no #Requires line) defining `ParseKV(text)` that returns a Map. Each line is key=value, lines separated by `n. Trim spaces around keys and values. Ignore blank lines, lines whose first non-space character is #, and lines without '='. A later duplicate key overrides an earlier one. Output only one autohotkey code block containing the complete file.
tasks.harness:
#Requires AutoHotkey v2.0
#Include solution.ahk
m := ParseKV("# c`n a = 1 `n`nb=two words`na=3`n  # x`nbad line`n")
ok := (m.Count = 2 && m["a"] = "3" && m["b"] = "two words")
FileAppend((ok ? "OK" : "FAIL") "`n", "*")
ExitApp

#Requires AutoHotkey v2.0
#Include solution.ahk
ok := (Average([2,4,6]) = 4 && Average([]) = 0)
FileAppend((ok ? "OK" : "FAIL") "`n", "*")
ExitApp
